races.name: Magners Original Cider Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sand Sea
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for David & Nicola Barron returning 14 days after finishing sixth and seventh on Good and Soft; similar-going form reads 0W0P from two attempts, and Paul Mulrennan will need late gaps to appear in a race likely to be run at a muddling pace.

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's hold-up type ridden by 5lb claimer Rhys Elliott, 10 days after finishing ninth on Soft and seventh on Good; the apprentice allowance could be an asset in a sprint finish but the horse has placed zero times from two starts and the pace scenario is unlikely to suit a true closer.

runners_data.name: Alpha Platoon
runners_data.note: Noel Wilson's three-year-old has only one run to its name, a seventh on Soft, and its natural hold-up inclination means Ryan Sexton will find it difficult to secure the rear berth it prefers when the field is already loaded with closers — it is effectively being asked to race in unfamiliar territory.

runners_data.name: Tide Runner
runners_data.note: Lightly raced unknown quantity for John & Sean Quinn with just a third over 5f on Good to go on; Billy Garritty may allow this horse to drift forward from its unclassified style, and that single piece of similar-going form (0W1P) makes it one of the few horses with any evidence of handling these conditions.

runners_data.name: Brash
runners_data.note: David & Nicola Barron's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type but is mapped to midfield because the field is saturated with closers; David Nolan is a smart tactical jockey, yet two runs of seventh on Soft and Soft/Good both returned no placed efforts, and racing closer to the pace than preferred is unlikely to unlock improvement.

runners_data.name: Star With Purpose
runners_data.note: Quinn's three-year-old carries a headgear flag (blinkers) and has placed once from three runs (6f Soft, 6f Good, 6f Soft), suggesting reasonable experience of this distance; the unknown style profile and headgear application could see Oisin McSweeney push forward early, making this a horse to watch for an unexpected prominent role.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up specialist has the most exposed form in the field — four placed efforts from five starts including two seconds over 6f on Good — and though mapped to midfield due to redistribution, Sean Kirrane's experience gives him the best chance of finding the ideal position in a muddling sprint; the Good-ground profile (4/5 similar-going runs) is the strongest in this field.

runners_data.name: Le Puy
runners_data.note: Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's three-year-old returns after 58 days off with a fourth on Good over 7f and a seventh on Soft over 6f; Cam Hardie is a capable northern jockey and the step back to 6f suits, though the absence needs noting and the hold-up style faces the same structural challenge as the rest of the closers here.

runners_data.name: Shatin Beauty
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's three-year-old is a complete unknown — no days-since-last-run recorded, no form string, no going assessment possible — and Aiden Brookes takes the ride; total opacity means this horse cannot be placed confidently in any scenario but could surprise in a chaotic race where unexposed types occasionally outrun their profile.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field, the early tempo is likely to be set by default rather than design, with Tide Runner and Star With Purpose — both unraced or lightly tested unknown quantities — potentially drifting forward from their uncertain style profiles, while the field bunches and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. The absence of a genuine pace-setter means the early fractions will likely be modest on Good ground at Ayr, compressing the field and making early position less critical than raw finishing speed in the closing stages. Sand Sea, Thistle Nil, Le Puy and Brash are all registered hold-up types, but with so many closers in the field and no horse willing to go hard from the front, those drawn handy and able to travel mid-division will benefit most from the resulting falsely-run dash. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses capable of producing a sharp, late burst from a compact midfield position — true off-the-pace closers will struggle to generate the separation they need in what will essentially be a sprint from home. The field carries more hold-up horses than the pace map can comfortably accommodate at the rear — Brash, Alpha Platoon and Stoneacre Joe are genuine hold-up types shown in midfield because they cannot all get to the back in this race shape, and the horse most likely to secure a prominent position by default is Tide Runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse commits early and the field crawls into a bunch sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If no horse commits early and the field crawls into a bunch sprint from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Default Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Tide Runner or Star With Purpose drift to the front unchallenged and set a sustainable, honest gallop.
scenarios.body: If Tide Runner or Star With Purpose drift to the front unchallenged and set a sustainable, honest gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and create a true test where horses coming from off the pace can mow down a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field out and create a true test where horses coming from off the pace can mow down a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Scrimmage No Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses jostle for position in the early stages, creating a ragged, stop-start tempo that unsettles the field.
scenarios.body: If multiple horses jostle for position in the early stages, creating a ragged, stop-start tempo that unsettles the field.

watchPoints.text: Stoneacre Joe has the strongest Good-ground profile in the field (4 from 5 similar-going runs, including two seconds over this exact 6f trip on Good) and Sean Kirrane must secure a clean, unobstructed run in what will be a heavily congested sprint finish — watch where he positions in the first furlong.

Shatin Beauty has no accessible form or going record and is entirely opaque — if Linda Perratt has prepared this horse specifically for this track and conditions, it could outrun its price in a weak maiden; monitor market moves in the final 30 minutes.

Star With Purpose is fitted with headgear and has an unclassified style — if Oisin McSweeney elects to push forward and grab a prominent rail position by default, the horse effectively becomes the de facto pace-setter in a race with no natural leader, fundamentally reshaping the entire race.

Alpha Platoon and Brash are both natural hold-up horses for the same trainer yard (Barron) and are mapped out of their preferred positions; if both jockeys attempt to drop out to the rear simultaneously, they risk getting blocked by each other and arriving at the finish without a clear passage — a legitimate traffic risk in the final furlong.

races.name: AU Signature Handicap

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Two wins from fifteen on Good ground and has shown ability over this 9f range; Lauren Young's 5lb claim is valuable at the weights, and Jim Goldie sends her out in decent nick (T14: 8/47) — she is a genuine hold-up horse who will need any uptick in tempo to land her late effort.

runners_data.name: Dingwall
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Iain Jardine who has placed twice at 9-10f on Good ground in recent starts; Cara Tuke's 7lb claim helps considerably at OR 61, and tracking Myrrh from a handy position suits this horse's natural style better than most rivals here.

runners_data.name: Tap Dancer
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who has struggled for a win lately (0W in last five, best a fourth on Good); 30 days since last run for Jim Goldie is notable, and the step into 10f territory has produced mixed results — needs a faster pace than Myrrh is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Elizabeth Bay
runners_data.note: Placed third on Good ground in recent form but is a true rear-of-field operator — Katie Scott's runner is effectively squeezed out of its preferred role by the weight of hold-up horses in this field, and its 0W from twelve Good-ground runs underlines the uphill task.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran for R Mike Smith with two wins in fifteen Good-ground starts; at OR 56 and 135lbs the weight is against him, and despite a handy third most recently, he is a natural hold-up horse denied his ideal position by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Off Spin
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (four placed from fifteen on Good, headgear: t) for Tim Easterby, with a third at 10f on Good last time; OR 55 and 134lbs is tough, and as a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield map position, he needs the race to be run at a clip Myrrh has no intention of setting.

runners_data.name: Myrrh
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner for David Nolan and David O'Meara (T14: 7/59); three-year-old at OR 65 — highest in the field — carrying 132lbs, with a win and two placed efforts at 8-10f on Good; controls the pace entirely and that dominance is both the race's key tactical fact and a double-edged sword if Nolan overestimates the lead needed.

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old won at 9f on Soft last time and placed at 8f Good; Conor Whiteley's 7lb claim keeps the weight manageable at 129lbs, and a prominent-hold-up blend (headgear: p) means he could sit just behind Myrrh and benefit most cleanly from the controlled tempo — form arrow pointing the right direction.

runners_data.name: Shifter
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Wilf Storey (T14: 0/2 — yard out of form) with one win from fifteen on Good; Paula Muir's 3lb claim provides minor compensation, but recent form reads 9-9854 and the horse is a deep hold-up type unable to get close to the pace in this configuration.

runners_data.name: Zebra Star
runners_data.note: Second R Mike Smith runner alongside Glasses Up; OR 46 is lowest in the field and five placed from fifteen on Good is the best that can be said — a natural hold-up horse carrying 125lbs who faces significant challenges simply getting competitive, let alone winning, in this company and race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Myrrh is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Nolan can control this race from the outset at a measured, sustainable gallop over 1m2f on Good turf at Ayr. The danger is that pace is not truly searching — a lone leader at a comfortable tempo over this trip typically sets up a race for prominent closers rather than deep hold-up horses who need a strong early fraction to bridge the gap late. This field is loaded with hold-up types — Elizabeth Bay, Glasses Up, Off Spin, Shifter, and Zebra Star are all genuine rearward runners forced into mapped midfield positions because the race shape simply cannot accommodate them all where they want to be — meaning their positional redistribution significantly undermines the likelihood of a closers' finish. The pace dynamic therefore strongly favours horses who travel prominently close to Myrrh, can track a measured gallop without burning energy, and have the scope to pick up in the straight — a prominent-to-midfield profile riding the controlled tempo is the clear beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Myrrh Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Myrrh dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the closers cannot generate enough sustained momentum from their wide-of-ideal positions.
scenarios.body: If Myrrh dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the closers cannot generate enough sustained momentum from their wide-of-ideal positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Myrrh Holds On Front
scenarios.trigger: If Myrrh's controlled lead is never seriously tested and she converts her dominant tactical position into a front-running victory under David Nolan.
scenarios.body: If Myrrh's controlled lead is never seriously tested and she converts her dominant tactical position into a front-running victory under David Nolan.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Breakaway Closer Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than anticipated and one of the genuinely good hold-up horses — Penelope's Sister or Off Spin — finds a gap and generates a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is slightly stronger than anticipated and one of the genuinely good hold-up horses — Penelope's Sister or Off Spin — finds a gap and generates a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Crowded Rear, No Room
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion among the many hold-up types causes interference, shuffling, or a race run in bunches that disrupts most of the field.
scenarios.body: If the congestion among the many hold-up types causes interference, shuffling, or a race run in bunches that disrupts most of the field.

watchPoints.text: Myrrh's unchallenged lead is the race's pivot — watch whether David Nolan chooses to quicken the tempo around the final bend or dawdles, as that single decision will determine whether closers can reach him or whether the race is already over.

Five genuine hold-up horses (Elizabeth Bay, Glasses Up, Off Spin, Shifter, Zebra Star) are all seeking the same rear positions — watch for crowding, shuffling, and potential interference on the descent into Ayr's home straight as riders jostle for daylight.

Fans Favourite's headgear (p — presumably a hood or similar) suggests a horse that can be keen — Conor Whiteley (7lb claimer) must manage that energy carefully if he is to hold a tracking position without burning out behind Myrrh before the turn.

Dingwall has placed twice at 9f on Good recently but has never won beyond 9f — the step to 10f (1m2f) is a marginal stamina question worth monitoring in the closing stages if the race does quicken late.
Jim Goldie saddles two runners (Penelope's Sister and Tap Dancer) — watch market moves between them in the hour before the race as a stable pointer to which the yard considers live.

races.name: Millar Callaghan Engineering Handicap

runners_data.name: The Gay Blade
runners_data.note: Trainer Iain Jardine is in fair form (3/41 over 14 days) and this seven-year-old has won twice at 7f on Good ground recently, with prominent racing style suiting a Black Storm-led tempo perfectly; ran just four days ago but clearly thriving.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Second last time out at 7f on Good and handled this trip well, though its true preference is to race from the back; with the field stacked with hold-up types it is unlikely to find the clean run it needs, tempering expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Imperial Guard
runners_data.note: Finishing positions of 8, 8, 6 in last three runs paint a tough picture, and although it ideally wants to close from behind, it won't get the deep field and strong pace needed to showcase that style here; sim-going record of 9 from 15 suggests limited impact on Good.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: 314 days off the track is an enormous question mark and this horse's form at the trip — including an 11th on Good ground — offers little encouragement; it wants to come from off the pace but the race shape is unlikely to produce a late-closing opportunity.

runners_data.name: Al Muqdad
runners_data.note: David Nolan is an experienced pilot and this horse has placed twice at 7f on Good, but the headgear note and a sim-going record of just 2 from 15 suggest it is a big price rather than a banker; shaped as a hold-up type, it needs pace and may not get enough.

runners_data.name: Ashen
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 7f on Good ground and Jim Goldie's yard is flying (8/47 over 14 days); though it races naturally from off the pace and is mapped forward due to redistribution, its recent winning form over this exact trip and conditions makes it one of the most interesting runners.

runners_data.name: Dorney Lake
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been at 6f and this is a step up to 7f, which is an untested angle; fitted with tongue-strap and cheekpieces, and its hold-up style is displaced here — a horse to treat with caution given the distance query.

runners_data.name: Black Storm
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner, winning the role of pace-setter by default; its recent form at 7f on Good (2nd, 4th, 4th) shows it stays competitive, and an uncontested lead is its optimal scenario, though the STYLE_FIT tag suggests it doesn't always finish off its races.

runners_data.name: Glorious Kitty
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 7f and 8f on Good ground are highly relevant, the trainer combination of Michael & David Easterby has decent 14-day form, and a sim-going record of 7/15 with 2 wins shows it can deliver on Good; capable of winning from any of the middle scenarios.

runners_data.name: Catalyse
runners_data.note: A fades-in-finish warning tag is damning, and a form string of 9-0007 confirms it has not threatened recently; two days since its last run and a Going Handicap mark of 'p' alongside a 10th on Good last time suggest this is a very difficult win to construct.

races.paceDynamic: Black Storm is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the gates at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over Ayr's flat seven furlongs, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead. The Gay Blade will press from a prominent position just off the pace, providing a degree of company without threatening to turn this into a true test of stamina. The five genuine hold-up horses — Novak, Imperial Guard, Defence Missile, Ashen, and Dorney Lake — have been pushed forward on the map because this field is saturated with hold-up types; of those, Ashen and Glorious Kitty carry the most convincing recent form to make an impact from off the pace, but the redistribution means few will find their natural rhythm at the rear. With one horse able to control fractions unchallenged and Good ground rewarding horses that travel smoothly, this race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track Black Storm and sprint past in the closing stages rather than horses needing a truly strong pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Black Storm Controls, Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Black Storm gets a clean break and dictates a sustainable tempo, allowing a prominent or tracking horse to peel off the pace and finish strongly.
scenarios.body: If Black Storm gets a clean break and dictates a sustainable tempo, allowing a prominent or tracking horse to peel off the pace and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Cuts Through
scenarios.trigger: If Black Storm goes just fast enough to stretch the field, allowing a horse with a strong turn of foot to close from midfield in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Black Storm goes just fast enough to stretch the field, allowing a horse with a strong turn of foot to close from midfield in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady and Black Storm is never pressured, conserving enough energy to resist challengers all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuinely steady and Black Storm is never pressured, conserving enough energy to resist challengers all the way to the line.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If Black Storm sets an unsustainably fast early gallop or something unexpected forces a contested pace, exhausting the front end.
scenarios.body: If Black Storm sets an unsustainably fast early gallop or something unexpected forces a contested pace, exhausting the front end.

watchPoints.text: Black Storm draws clear framing: if Ryan Sexton gets a clean break and Black Storm bowls along uncontested, every other runner is effectively chasing — watch for the gap to the field in the first furlong as the key early signal.

Ashen (Paul Mulrennan) won last time over this exact trip on Good ground and Jim Goldie's 8/47 14-day strike rate demands respect — watch whether Mulrennan manages to find a prominent position despite the natural hold-up tendencies, as that would significantly boost its chance.

Glorious Kitty (Lewis Chalkley, 7lb claim) carries back-to-back winning form over 7-8f on Good ground and has the profile to land this from a tracking position — the 7lb claim is notable and could be the difference at the weights in a competitive handicap.

The cluster of genuine hold-up horses (Novak, Imperial Guard, Dorney Lake, Defence Missile) all competing for similar wide or rear berths creates traffic risk in the straight — watch for pocket trouble at the two-furlong pole if the pace eases and multiple horses simultaneously attempt to challenge.

Defence Missile's 314-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — if it returns with a fitness edge under Finlay Bassett (7lb), it could outrun its price, but an outright win first time back from that layoff would be a significant feat.

races.name: Tennent's Lager Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: In-form David O'Meara runner with back-to-back placed efforts on good ground at 10f, stepping into a front-running role here after a short 15-day turnaround; the STYLE_FIT flag indicates he is racing slightly out of his most natural position, but the absence of rivals willing to contest the lead makes this a viable tactical assignment.

runners_data.name: Cisco Disco
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old carrying a six-race winning streak before his last disappointing run, and three consecutive victories on soft and heavy give a slight going-preference concern on today's good surface; trainer R Mike Smith has a modest 14-day strike rate (2/19) and the 30-day absence warrants monitoring, but the prior form profile keeps him relevant if the good ground poses no issue.

runners_data.name: Livonian
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who showed a career-best effort with a win at 8f on good for Barry Murtagh, with headgear noted and a 15-day turnaround; the step back up to 10f from recent outings and a modest trainer 14-day record (0/2) are mild concerns, though good-ground form is present in his history.

runners_data.name: Star Cast
runners_data.note: Consistent and in-form prominent racer with four wins and two places from his last six runs, including victories at 10f on good and soft; Gemma Tutty's 14-day record (1/20) is low-volume but the horse's own profile is the compelling factor, and the 7lb claimer Jake Dickson creates a useful weight concession in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose recent form over extreme trips (16f, 17f) is notably longer than today's 10f, suggesting this is a compression back to a sharper test; the 12-day jockey change flag is worth noting, and while he has placed at 17f on good ground, his form at this shorter trip is limited in the recent record.

runners_data.name: Dwindling Funds
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old is a genuine front-runner by nature, but the field's prominent surplus means he is unlikely to secure his preferred early berth and will be asked to race with more restraint than suits him; recent form figures of 62-200 reflect a horse that has dropped out of form, and the 37-day break adds uncertainty, though three career wins on good-going conditions keep him in the equation if he rediscovers his best.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old whose last five starts have produced a sequence of double-digit finishes, with finishing positions of 12, 10, 8, 4, 4 suggesting deep-closing profile that rarely gets competitive at this level; headgear noted, and while Amie Waugh's 3lb claim helps with the weight, the consistent poor finishing positions on good ground are hard to overlook.

runners_data.name: Pol Roger
runners_data.note: Produced an eye-catching second at 10f on good ground 17 days ago as his best recent effort, having run poorly over shorter trips since; Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim assists, and the return to 10f on a matching surface gives this hold-up type a clear chance of repeating his placed effort, though the overall record on good going (0W3P) suggests a placer's profile.

runners_data.name: Molinari
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old making a significant return from a 188-day absence, with all five recent starts on standard/artificial and no turf good-ground experience in the recent record; the lengthy layoff is a serious fitness question, and while he has placed at 10f on standard, today's surface and conditions represent a step into the unknown for Martin Todhunter's veteran.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old who has won or placed in all three career starts on good ground (1W2P), winning last time out at 8f good — the sharpest recent form in the field on a matching surface; Lauren Young's 5lb claim provides a weight advantage, but the horse is a natural prominent racer who will be asked to race further back than ideal given the congested early positions, which is the primary risk to her chance.

races.paceDynamic: Obito is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, David Nolan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 1m2f on good ground at Ayr. The field carries a glut of naturally prominent horses — Dwindling Funds, Molinari, and Sanafi Zabeel are all true front-to-midfield types who will be squeezed out of their preferred position by the sheer volume of similar runners, meaning they will be forced to race in a more restrained, midfield role against their instincts. Star Cast, Cisco Disco, and Livonian complete a prominent group that will jostle for the positions immediately behind Obito, likely creating a compact early order with no genuine pace injection to stretch the field. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner, a competitive but controlled early pace, and a field unable to assert its natural rhythm — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently with cover and produce a sustained late effort, rather than either extreme of true pace-setters or deep closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Obito Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Obito is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets an honest but unspectacular pace, the race becomes a test for horses who travel prominently and pick up strongly in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Obito is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets an honest but unspectacular pace, the race becomes a test for horses who travel prominently and pick up strongly in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early prominent battle for position burns more energy than expected and the pace fractionally quickens mid-race, horses tracking from just off the pace will arrive fresh in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the early prominent battle for position burns more energy than expected and the pace fractionally quickens mid-race, horses tracking from just off the pace will arrive fresh in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Outstays
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely dawdling and the field clusters in a tight bunch, Obito's front-running position becomes a major tactical asset as he kicks into the straight unchallenged.
scenarios.body: If the gallop is genuinely dawdling and the field clusters in a tight bunch, Obito's front-running position becomes a major tactical asset as he kicks into the straight unchallenged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Prominent Horse Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the true prominent types — Dwindling Funds, Sanafi Zabeel, or Molinari — manages to secure a better position than their redistribution suggests and travels in their natural front-to-midfield comfort zone.
scenarios.body: If one of the true prominent types — Dwindling Funds, Sanafi Zabeel, or Molinari — manages to secure a better position than their redistribution suggests and travels in their natural front-to-midfield comfort zone.

watchPoints.text: Sanafi Zabeel's three-from-three record on good going is the sharpest surface-specific form in the race, but watch whether Lauren Young can secure a forward position early — if she is shuffled back into a true hold-up role against her nature, that form edge is significantly compromised.

Star Cast's 7lb claimer Jake Dickson is riding a horse in form in a race where weight matters in a handicap — watch for whether Dickson can hold a prominent position through the early scramble for spots, as getting caught wide or losing ground could neutralise the form advantage.

Molinari's 188-day absence and all-weather-only recent form mean his fitness and ability to handle good turf going is genuinely unknown — watch his pre-race behaviour and early travelling for signs of a handicapper returning in shape versus one needing the run.

Obito's ability to control the pace without being pressed is the fulcrum of most scenarios — watch how aggressively, if at all, any of the prominent group (Cisco Disco, Livonian) attempt to close him down in the first two furlongs, as any sustained pressure on the leader would materially shift which scenario plays out.

Jim Goldie saddles three runners (Dwindling Funds, Spanish Hustle, Sanafi Zabeel) — watch for any stable form pattern on the day, as a trainer running multiple horses in the same race occasionally creates tactical riding instructions that alter expected pace positions.

races.name: Outcider Handicap

runners_data.name: Approaching Dawn
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground last time out suggesting this 1m trip is within range, though as a genuine hold-up type his redistribution to midfield means he may struggle to find his natural rhythm in what is set to be a slowly-run race; Jim Goldie in good recent form (8/47 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Walk On Walk On
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has failed to finish closer than fourth in recent starts; headgear noted and the step back from 7f distances is the key angle to watch, though as a true hold-up horse placed into midfield by the race shape, the lack of a genuine pace to chase into makes this look a difficult assignment.

runners_data.name: Flying Moonlight
runners_data.note: Returns from a 261-day absence for Sandy Thomson, who has had only two runners in the past fortnight; three career runs all produced seventh-place finishes and with no experience beyond 7f this step to a mile is unproven — the lengthy layoff is the dominant concern here regardless of running style.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Style is listed as unknown which is a useful wild card — Oisin McSweeney takes the ride for trainer Katie Scott and if this lightly-raced three-year-old can be placed handily it could suit a slowly-run race; all form has come at 7f so the mile extension is the question mark on what is otherwise a lightly exposed profile.

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Consistently places — three seconds and a third in his last five starts including twice at this 8f trip on standard/good — and Andrew Mullen knows this horse well; suited by tracking a pace-setter and producing a late effort, the lone front-runner scenario is close to ideal for his style, though his best going form is on softer than today's good.

runners_data.name: Golden Valour
runners_data.note: A decade-old veteran whose headgear is retained; has placed 10 times from 15 runs on similar going which speaks to consistency, but as a genuine hold-up type displaced to midfield by the crowded rear of the field, a slowly-run 1m handicap on good ground is not his most favourable scenario.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: Has been running over extreme distances (16-20f) recently and this drop back to 1m looks a significant change of plan — the question is whether he retains enough speed for this sharper test; David Nolan is an upgrade in the saddle and the trainer has two winners from 19 runners over the past fortnight, giving this a measure of stable confidence despite the trip query.

runners_data.name: Rory's Gold
runners_data.note: Apprentice Amie Waugh (3lb claim) takes the ride and at 141lbs he is one of the bigger weights in the race; form shows a mix of trips from 7f to 10f with no win and no place on going faster than standard, so the good ground today is worth flagging as a potential concern.

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: The sole pace-setter returning from a 399-day absence, though his Ayr record on good ground is excellent (2 wins and 8 places from 12 similar-going runs); the long layoff is the obvious caveat but Jim Goldie's yard is in form and Paul Mulrennan knows how to exploit an uncontested lead — the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that his chance is most dependent on the solo-lead scenario materialising rather than any other shape.

races.paceDynamic: Braes Of Doune is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over Ayr's flat mile, and with no other horse likely to seriously contest the lead, Paul Mulrennan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off. The remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up types — Hunterian, Mayor Of Maghera, Rory's Gold, Approaching Dawn, Walk On Walk On, Flying Moonlight and Golden Valour all prefer to race off the pace — meaning the race will be strung out behind a lone pace-setter with little pressure applied through the early and middle stages. This field holds significantly more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Walk On Walk On, Golden Valour, Flying Moonlight and Approaching Dawn are all redistributed to midfield positions they would not naturally choose, meaning the actual bunch behind Braes Of Doune will be compact rather than truly strung out. With a lone front-runner setting a gentle, uncontested tempo on good ground, this race shape strongly favours horses with tactical versatility and a turn of foot who can track the leader in a position to pounce, rather than pure closers who need a true gallop to close into.

scenarios.body: If the early pace is so slow that the field bunches tightly and the race becomes a sprint from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp Leader

scenarios.body: If several of the redistributed hold-up types push forward unexpectedly and inject enough pace to stretch the field, allowing true closers to come from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wins Wire To Wire

scenarios.body: If Braes Of Doune, fresh after a 399-day absence, bowls along at a strong enough pace that the hold-up field simply cannot close the gap on good ground.

watchPoints.text: Braes Of Doune's 399-day absence is the single biggest variable in the race — if he returns short of full fitness he may be caught in the straight having set the only pace, collapsing the scenario the whole race shape is built around.

Hunterian has finished second or third in four of his last five starts and consistently performs when tracking a pace-setter — watch whether Andrew Mullen slots him into second or third behind Braes Of Doune from the off, as that is the position this race shape rewards most.

Mayor Of Maghera's drastic drop from 16-20f trips back to 1m is unexplained by the data — if the stable has identified a specific reason for the trip change, David Nolan's booking suggests this is intended as a serious run rather than a convenience start.

Several hold-up horses (Walk On Walk On, Golden Valour, Flying Moonlight, Approaching Dawn) are redistributed into midfield positions; watch the early stages to see whether any push forward unexpectedly — if two or more do, the pace dynamic changes materially and the slowly-run scenario is invalidated.

Carmel Valley's unknown running style is worth tracking from the gate — if Oisin McSweeney positions this lightly-raced three-year-old prominently early, it could represent a deliberate tactical switch that upgrades the horse's chance in what is otherwise a hold-up-dominated field.

races.name: Mills Milk Scotland Handicap

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner here, with back-to-back wins over 16-17f on good ground underlining her suitability for this exact trip and surface; Conor Whiteley (7lb claim) retains the ride, and her visor (hg:v) is in place — having run just yesterday (LR:1d), bounce-back risk is the only credible flag against her dominating from the front.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes the ride for Jim Goldie, a trainer firing at 8/47 in the past 14 days; a genuine hold-up horse whose best recent form includes a win at 16f and a placed effort at 13f on good, making him one of the more credentialled closers if the pace is strong enough to aim at.

runners_data.name: Ned Broy
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's five-year-old is fitted with a hood (hg:p) and has placed form over 11f on good but his last three runs over longer trips on softer ground have been poor — 17 days since last run is fine, but his sim-going record of just 0W1P from nine good-ground starts is a concern for confidence.

runners_data.name: Fleur De Mer
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's mare returns after 73 days off (LR:73d), a layoff that introduces fitness doubt, and her best form comes on easier ground and standard surfaces with 0W0P from 15 good-ground attempts; a natural hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield reflects the glut of closers in this field rather than any change in her tactical approach.

runners_data.name: Billy No Mates
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old veteran for Michael Dods whose placed efforts include seconds and thirds at 14-16f, including a third on good ground last time; he races hold-up by nature but is shown in midfield purely because the field is overloaded with closers — his age and 0W15 good-ground win record suggest place rather than win.

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old carries the Amie Waugh 3lb claim and boasts genuine stamina, with two wins over 13-15f on softer ground, though sim-going returns 0W1P from five good-ground runs; held up by nature and mapped to midfield only because there are too many hold-up horses for the shape — still worth tracking in a scenario where pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Ewan Whillans' nine-year-old wears a tongue-tie and hood (hg:tp) and has been placed at 16f on soft but shows a weak recent profile of 839-74 with 0W1P on good ground; a true hold-up horse whose map position in midfield reflects redistribution — at this age and on this going his chance looks slim.

runners_data.name: Angelardo
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey's four-year-old was last out 11 days ago and showed a second at 16f on standard ground last time, suggesting stamina isn't in doubt; true running style is hold-up but he ends up in midfield here because the closers outnumber available rear slots — at OR=50 he's lightly weighted and his youth gives him improvement scope.

runners_data.name: La Tosca
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old steps up sharply in trip to 1m7f having run only up to 1m4f so far, which is a significant unknown — she has placed on good ground and showed consistent form figures of 4342, but the step to staying distances for the first time against older horses is the key risk factor in her favour or against.

races.paceDynamic: Laravie is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 1m7f handicap and should stride into a clear, uncontested lead from the off, setting what figures to be a sustainable, measured gallop on good ground at Ayr. With no genuine pace rival to challenge her through the early and middle stages, she will control tempo entirely, likely leaving the entire field in a waiting game behind her as she dictates from the front. The field behind is dominated by hold-up types — Gallus Norman, Ned Broy, Fleur De Mer, Billy No Mates, Aighear, Ebony Maw, Angelardo, and La Tosca all favour coming from off the pace — but several are redistributed to midfield simply because there are too many true closers to map at the rear, and they will not get their natural position in this shape. With Laravie able to roll along unchallenged and set her own rhythm, this race shape strongly favours a prominent, front-running profile or a horse capable of travelling just off the sole leader before kicking — pure hold-up horses dependent on a strong pace to aim at are disadvantaged here.

watchPoints.text: Laravie has raced just one day ago (LR:1d) — watch her closely in the paddock and at the start for any signs of fatigue or stiffness, as a bounce here could unravel the entire pace map.

La Tosca is attempting 1m7f for the first time having never run beyond 1m4f — if she fails to settle or weakens badly turning in, it could create interference for the hold-up horses making ground behind her.

With five horses redistributed from hold-up to midfield, the middle of the pack may become congested in the early stages — watch for Fleur De Mer, Ebony Maw, and Angelardo jostling for position and potentially blocking each other's runs entering the straight.

Gallus Norman is paired with Paul Mulrennan for trainer Jim Goldie who also runs Aighear in the same race — watch for any stable tactics that influence which of the two is given more favourable positioning, as Mulrennan's experience could prove decisive if pace is strong enough.

races.name: Good Luck Scotland Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Nala The Lioness
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer whose best form (win over 12f on Soft) came from the rear; held up by true style but the overcrowded hold-up division means she is unlikely to get the position she needs, tempering her prospects in a sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Another Beautiful
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has one placed effort on a similar surface (1/14 sim-going) and not run for 101 days, which is a significant freshness concern; races from hold-up position and the 1m5f trip is within range, but the lengthy absence is the dominant query.

runners_data.name: Desert Quest
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with solid placed form at 12f on Good (4/12f/GOO) and a recent run 17 days ago keeping him fit; hold-up style suits a truly-run race and his four placed efforts on similar going make him one of the more consistent profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose best effort was a second on Good over 12f, and while that form is relevant, a visor is worn and the horse's true hold-up style sees it shuffled into midfield on the map where it will race out of its natural comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Freak Encounter
runners_data.note: Young hold-up performer with no wins or placed efforts on this type of going in 15 attempts on similar surfaces, which is a stark negative; bumped from its natural rearward position by the overcrowded hold-up section, it faces a stiff ask to land a blow here.

runners_data.name: Is She Now
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced veteran who has run 128 days ago and had a 46-day jockey absence flag, with a form string showing a distant 18th over 18f on Good as the most recent effort; the staying trip helps in theory but the layoff and poor recent form are significant negatives.

runners_data.name: Late Claim
runners_data.note: Has raced exclusively at 12f on Soft or Standard, so the step up to Good ground over 1m5f is an untested combination; sits on a modest sim-going record of 1/15 and its natural hold-up style is displaced by the crowded field, limiting tactical options.

runners_data.name: Tracker Issue
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field on OR=50 with a second over 16f on Good as recent form (4/16f/GOO), suggesting the trip and conditions are comfortably within scope; most likely to push forward given the lack of confirmed front-runners and could dictate terms if connections allow.

runners_data.name: Star Of Emerald
runners_data.note: The sole runner with an unknown style tag, a lightly-framed three-year-old carrying the lowest weight (120lbs) and trained by Edward Bethell whose 14-day record (4/24) suggests reasonable stable form; the style uncertainty is the key variable — if this runner goes forward, it could exploit the absence of genuine leaders.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m5f contest at Ayr is set to begin at a crawling or moderate tempo, with the pace evolving organically from a cluster of hold-up types rather than being set by a genuine leader. Star Of Emerald (style unknown) and Tracker Issue are the most likely to push forward from their respective positions, but neither is a confirmed pace-setter, meaning the early gallop will be tentative and the field likely to bunch together through the middle stages. The race will almost certainly compress into a sprint-style finish in the final two furlongs, favouring horses with a turn of foot rather than those needing true staying tests. This shape best suits runners who can travel midfield and produce a sustained late run — though the redistribution of multiple true hold-up types (Nala The Lioness, Falaise Blanc, Late Claim, Freak Encounter, Is She Now) to the midfield mapping means the race will be even more congested centrally than the pace map suggests, with those horses unlikely to achieve their natural rearward positions; whoever can most efficiently navigate a slow-run, tactical finish from a handy berth holds the clearest advantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tracker Issue to push forward from the outset — as the highest-rated horse (OR=50) with proven form over 16f on Good, if it secures the lead unchallenged in a hold-up-heavy field it could prove very hard to peg back.

Star Of Emerald's style is unclassified — monitor its behaviour at the start and in the early stages, as any forward move from this lightweight three-year-old could fundamentally alter the pace shape from flag-fall.

The severe overcrowding of hold-up types (Nala The Lioness, Falaise Blanc, Late Claim, Freak Encounter, Is She Now all displaced to midfield) creates a significant traffic risk in the straight — horses drawn wider or with the clearest passage are at a premium.

Another Beautiful is returning from a 101-day absence for Ivan Furtado whose 14-day strike rate is 1/38 — monitor her in the parade ring and early market moves for any signs the stable believes she is ready to run to her best fresh.

The going has remained consistently Good across all seven races at Ayr today, providing a reliable and fair surface — no runner should be disadvantaged by ground deterioration, meaning form on Good should be given full weight in assessments.
